festivals: Yama Dwitiya / Bhai Dooj (annual closing ceremony)

history.summary: One of the four temples of the Char Dham Yatra (traditionally the first visited), located at about 3,293 m in the Garhwal Himalayas near the source of the Yamuna River. The present temple was built in the 19th century by Maharani Guleria of Jaipur and later rebuilt by Maharaja Pratap Shah of Tehri Garhwal after damage by natural calamities. The sanctum holds a black marble idol of Goddess Yamuna, said to have bathed daily with the Ganga when sage Asit Muni lived here; the priests come from Kharsali village. Nearby hot springs (notably Surya Kund) are used to cook rice and potatoes offered as prasadam, and the sacred Divya Shila rock pillar is worshipped before entering. The temple opens each year on Akshaya Tritiya and closes on Bhai Dooj; during winter the idol is moved to Kharsali village.

name: Yamunotri Temple
town_description: Yamunotri is the mountain pilgrimage site at the source of the Yamuna River in Uttarkashi district, sitting at about 3,293 m beneath the Bandarpunch peak. Reached by a 6 km trek from Janki Chatti, it is the traditional starting point of the Char Dham Yatra, known for its hot springs, the Divya Shila and the Champasar Glacier further uphill.

travel.airport: Jolly Grant Airport, Dehradun, about 200 km
travel.railway: Dehradun or Rishikesh railway stations, then road to Janki Chatti
travel.road: Road up to Janki Chatti (via Dehradun-Barkot); then a 6 km trek to the temple, with ponies and palanquins available

visitor_information.best_time: May to mid-June and mid-September to October, within the open season (Akshaya Tritiya to Bhai Dooj)
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily during the open season (April/May to October/November); closed in winter due to snowfall
